title: Monitoring service has no authorization check
body:
`MonitoringServiceServer.GetSystemStatus` and `StreamSystemMetrics` are reachable by any client with a valid mTLS cert, including `viewer`. The service is constructed without an auth dependency, so there is
   no per-method authorization check.

- `internal/joblet/server/monitoring_service.go`:38–83 , both methods, no s.auth.Authorized(ctx, ...) calls.                                                                                              
- `internal/joblet/server/grpc_server.go` , `NewMonitoringServiceServer` is constructed without `GRPCAuthorization`.

A holder of a `viewer` cert streams continuous host `CPU/memory/process/disk/network` metrics, enabling activity profiling of the daemon and its job scheduling.

title: JOBLET_CI_MODE=true disables all isolation in production builds
body:
If the daemon's environment contains `JOBLET_CI_MODE=true`, `executeCICommand` is used instead of the normal coordinator. This skips `PID/mount/IPC/UTS` namespaces, cgroup assignment, chroot, and privilege 
  dropping. Jobs run directly in the daemon's process tree as root.

in `internal/joblet/core/job_executor.go`:126 and 127 , branch on `JOBLET_CI_MODE`.


**scenario** : Anything that can set this env var on the daemon (misconfigured deployment, IAM-controlled SSM parameter store, compromised orchestrator) nullifies isolation for every subsequent job.                 
   
`executeCICommand` also skips path-traversal validation on uploaded files (`internal/joblet/core/job_executor.go`:166–179 joins `upload.Path` with `workDir` without `validation.ValidatePathWithinBase`).

title: runtime-build job type bypasses privilege drop and network isolation; controlled by client env var
body:
The `runtime-build` job type skips privilege drop, omits `CLONE_NEWNET`, and `bind-mounts` the host `filesystem`. It is selected by reading `JOB_TYPE` from the `client-supplied` Environment map, which means any  
  authenticated admin cert holder can submit a job that runs as host root with host network access.


  - `internal/joblet/server/job_service.go`:173 , server reads `JOB_TYPE` from client Environment, sets `jobType = domain.JobTypeRuntimeBuild`.                                                                 
  - `internal/joblet/core/unprivileged/namespace.go`:59 , privilege drop is skipped for `runtime-build`.
  - `internal/joblet/core/unprivileged/namespace.go`:42 , `CLONE_NEWUSER` is not set.                                                                                                                         
  - `internal/modes/jobexec/jobexec.go`:183 , execution branch.
  - `internal/joblet/core/filesystem/isolator.go`:342–388 , SetupBuilder bind-mounts host `fs` minus `/opt/joblet`.   


  **Attack scenario:** A holder of any `admin` cert submits a job with `Environment["JOB_TYPE"]="runtime-build"` and an arbitrary command. The job runs as root on the host with host networking, effectively root shell on the    
  daemon host.

title: Config silently re-loaded inside chroot in init-mode children, falls back to built-in defaults
body:
In the init-mode child process, `pkg/config.LoadConfig()` is called a second (and third) time after the chroot has been set up. The config file is not visible inside the chroot, so `LoadConfig` silently  
  returns built-in defaults - overwriting whatever values the operator configured in `joblet-config.yml`. The daemon and its init-mode child then disagree on filesystem paths, runtime base path, etc.
   

The `isolation.go` call site is the worst because even a malformed YAML file is silently ignored.

title: Fix Runtime Build on EC2/Cloud Instances
body:
## Summary

  - Fix DNS setup failure on EC2/systemd instances where /etc/resolv.conf is a symlink
  - Add automatic deadsnakes PPA fallback for Python 3.10+ packages on older Ubuntu
  - Fix documentation to reflect correct flat runtime directory structure

## Problem

  Runtime builds failed on EC2 instances with two issues:

  1. DNS setup failure:
  failed to write resolv.conf: open /tmp/.../merged/etc/resolv.conf: no such file or directory
  On EC2/systemd systems, /etc/resolv.conf is a symlink to /run/systemd/resolve/stub-resolv.conf. In the OverlayFS, this symlink exists but the target doesn't, causing WriteFile to fail.

  2. Python 3.11 not found:
  package not found: python3.11
  Python 3.10+ packages aren't available in default Ubuntu repos on older LTS versions.

## Solution

  DNS Fix (pkg/builder/isolation.go)
  - Detect broken symlinks by attempting to read the file content
  - Remove existing broken symlink before writing real resolv.conf
  - Use host's DNS config (following symlinks) or fallback to Google DNS

  Deadsnakes PPA (pkg/builder/isolation.go, pkg/builder/installer.go)
  - Skip strict validation for Python 3.10+ packages that may need PPA
  - Try installing from default repos first (works on Ubuntu 22.04+)
  - Automatically add deadsnakes PPA if package not found
  - All PPA changes occur in OverlayFS upper layer - host unchanged

title: add OverlayFS-Based Isolation for Runtime Builds
body:
Summary

  This PR implements OverlayFS-based isolation for runtime builds to ensure the host system is never contaminated during package installation. Previously, apt-get install and other package managers ran directly on the host, which could leave unw
anted packages and modifications on the system.

  Problem

  When building runtimes (e.g., rnx runtime build python-3.11-ml), system packages were installed directly on the host machine. This caused:
  - Host system contamination with build dependencies
  - Potential package conflicts with existing host software
  - Difficulty cleaning up after failed builds
  - Security concerns about untrusted package scripts modifying the host

  Solution

  Implemented OverlayFS-based chroot isolation:

```
Lower Layer (read-only):  /  (host root)      
Upper Layer (read-write): /tmp/rnx-isolation-XXXXX/upper
Merged View:              /tmp/rnx-isolation-XXXXX/merged 
```

  1. Setup: Mount OverlayFS with host root as read-only lower layer
  2. Install: Run package managers inside chroot targeting merged view
  3. Copy: Extract installed binaries/libraries from upper layer to runtime directory
  4. Cleanup: Unmount overlay and remove temp directory

title: Runtime build
body:
## Summary

  Replace deprecated GitHub-based runtime installation with a new declarative YAML-based builder that executes remotely on the Joblet server via gRPC.

  - Add `pkg/builder/` package with 14-phase build pipeline
  - Add `BuildRuntime` streaming RPC for remote builds with progress
  - Update `rnx runtime build` to use gRPC instead of local execution
  - Remove deprecated `pkg/registry/` and runtime installer code

  ## Motivation

  The previous runtime installation system downloaded pre-built runtimes from GitHub releases, which was inflexible and required maintaining a separate runtime repository. The new declarative builder allows users to define custom runtimes with a simple YAML specification that gets built directly on the Joblet server.

  ## Changes

  ### New Features
  - **Declarative YAML specification** - Define runtimes with `runtime.yaml` files
  - **14-phase build pipeline** - Parse, validate, install packages, copy binaries, generate config
  - **Language profiles** - Built-in support for Python, Java, Node.js, Go, Rust
  - **Pre/post-install hooks** - Custom scripts with configurable timeout
  - **Progress streaming** - Real-time build progress via gRPC

  ### Breaking Changes
  - `rnx runtime install <name>` replaced with `rnx runtime build <path>`
  - Runtimes now built from YAML specs instead of downloaded from registry

  ### Removed
  - `pkg/registry/` - GitHub registry client
  - `internal/joblet/core/runtime_installer.go` - Old installer
  - `InstallRuntime` method from `RuntimeService` interface

  ## Example Usage

  ```yaml
  # runtime.yaml
  schema_version: "1.0"
  name: python-3.11-ml
  version: 1.0.0
  description: Python 3.11 with ML packages

  base:
    language: python
    version: "3.11"

  pip:
    - numpy
    - pandas
    - scikit-learn

  # Build runtime on remote server
  rnx runtime build ./runtime.yaml

  # Use the runtime
  rnx job run --runtime=python-3.11-ml python -c "import numpy; print(numpy.__version__)"

title: rnx job log - Gap Scenario
body:
When using `rnx job log <JOB_ID>`, there was a potential gap in log streaming when transitioning from historical logs (
joblet-persist) to live logs (joblet-core on).

```
Timeline:
T0: Job produces logs 1-50 → buffer + persist
T1: rnx connects, queries persist (gets logs 1-50)
T2: Job produces logs 51-60 → buffer (not yet in persist)
T3: persist receives logs 51-60 via IPC
T4: rnx connects to joblet-core buffer
T5: Buffer returns logs 1-70 (ALL logs, including 1-50 already shown)
    Problem: Logs 51-60 appear twice (duplicate)
    OR if buffer cleared: Logs 51-60 might be missed (gap)
```

### Root Cause

1. **Buffer has no sequence tracking**: The in-memory buffer in joblet-core stores raw byte chunks without sequence
   numbers
2. **GetJobLogs returns unsequenced data**: The gRPC response (`DataChunk`) contains only payload bytes, no metadata
3. **IPC adds sequences separately**: Sequence numbers are only added when forwarding to persist via IPC
4. **No coordination**: No mechanism to tell joblet-core "start from sequence N+1"

title: Extract Admin UI into standalone `joblet-admin` package
body:
### Problem Statement

The admin UI is currently embedded within the RNX CLI, creating unnecessary complexity:

- **Node.js Dependency**: RNX binary requires Node.js just for the admin UI feature
- **Performance Issues**: Admin server spawns RNX CLI subprocesses instead of using direct gRPC
- **Distribution Overhead**: Homebrew formula must handle Node.js detection/installation
- **Coupling**: Web UI functionality is tightly coupled with CLI tool

### Proposed Solution

Create **`joblet-admin`** as a standalone npm package with direct protobuf/gRPC integration:

```
joblet-admin/
├── src/
│   ├── grpc/           # Direct gRPC client with mTLS
│   ├── server/         # Express + WebSocket server  
│   └── ui/             # React frontend
└── package.json
```

**Key Design Decision**: No separate `joblet-sdk-node` - the admin package will include its own gRPC client implementation. This avoids over-engineering since the admin UI is likely the only Node.js consumer.

### Benefits

- ✅ **Simplified RNX**: Becomes a pure Go binary with no Node.js dependencies
- ✅ **Better Performance**: Direct gRPC communication instead of CLI subprocess calls
- ✅ **Easier Installation**: 
  - RNX: Simple binary download
  - Admin: `npm install -g joblet-admin`
- ✅ **Independent Deployment**: Admin UI can be updated without RNX releases
- ✅ **Cleaner Architecture**: Clear separation between CLI and web UI
- ✅ **Docker Ready**: Can easily containerize the admin UI

### Implementation Plan

1. [ ] Set up new `joblet-admin` repository/package
2. [ ] Generate TypeScript protobuf bindings from `.proto` files
3. [ ] Implement gRPC client with mTLS support (using existing RNX config format)
4. [ ] Migrate admin server to use direct gRPC instead of CLI spawning
5. [ ] Move admin UI (React) and server code to new package
6. [ ] Publish to npm registry
7. [ ] Remove `rnx admin` command and related code from RNX
8. [ ] Update Homebrew formula (remove Node.js handling)
9. [ ] Update documentation

### Technical Details

- **gRPC Client**: Direct protobuf communication with joblet server
- **Config**: Reuse existing `~/.rnx/rnx-config.yml` format for compatibility
- **Entry Point**: `joblet-admin` command launches Express server with UI
- **Streaming**: WebSocket/SSE for real-time logs and metrics
- **No SDK Layer**: Intentionally avoiding separate SDK package (YAGNI principle)

### Migration Path

Users currently using `rnx admin` will need to:
```bash
# Before
rnx admin

# After  
npm install -g joblet-admin
joblet-admin
```

### Future Considerations

- If Node.js SDK is needed later, the gRPC client code can be extracted from joblet-admin
- Potential for Electron desktop app or hosted SaaS version
- Could add authentication layer for multi-user deployments

body:
## Summary

This document outlines the architectural design for transitioning Joblet from sequential integer job IDs to UUID-based identification using **native Linux kernel features**. The design ensures **complete immunity to race conditions** and supports **unlimited concurrent job creation** without any synchronization overhead.

### Critical Requirements
- **Race Condition Immunity**: Zero synchronization required between concurrent job creators
- **Unlimited Concurrency**: Support thousands of simultaneous job creations
- **Zero External Dependencies**: Use only native Linux kernel capabilities
- **Atomic Migration**: Single-phase cutover from JobId to JobUuid
- **No Persistence Layer**: Eliminate all state management complexity

## Problem Statement

### Concurrency Bottlenecks

Current Synchronization Requirements:
- Memory barrier on every access   
- CPU cache line bouncing          
- Lock contention at high load     
-  Persistence sync delays          

Performance Impact:
- 1 thread:     50ns per ID
- 10 threads:   500ns per ID (10x degradation)
- 100 threads:  5µs per ID (100x degradation)
- 1000 threads: 50µs per ID (1000x degradation)

## Native Linux UUID Solution Architecture

### Kernel-Level Concurrency Handling

Kernel Guarantees:
- Each read returns unique UUID (kernel-managed entropy pool)
- No thread coordination required
- No locks, no atomics, no barriers
- Cryptographically secure randomness
- Zero collision probability (2^122 random bits)

### Linux Kernel Implementation Details

## Concurrent Job Creation Flow

### Race Condition Immunity Proof

```
SCENARIO: 10,000 Concurrent Job Creations
─────────────────────────────────────────────

Traditional Sequential ID:
├── Needs: Global lock or atomic operation
├── Result: Contention, degraded performance
├── Risk: Counter corruption, ID collision
└── Failure Mode: Duplicate IDs, lost jobs

Native Linux UUID:
├── Needs: Nothing (kernel handles everything)
├── Result: Linear scaling with CPU cores
├── Risk: None (2^122 collision space)
└── Failure Mode: None (mathematically impossible)

Mathematical Proof:
─────────────────────
UUID v4 has 122 random bits
Collision probability for N UUIDs:
  P(collision) ≈ N² / 2^123

For 1 billion UUIDs:
  P(collision) ≈ 10^18 / 10^37 ≈ 10^-19

For 1 trillion UUIDs:
  P(collision) ≈ 10^24 / 10^37 ≈ 10^-13

```
**Conclusion: Collisions are impossible in practice**

# Joblet Network - Simplified Phase 1 Design

## Core Concept
**Four network types**: `none`, `isolated`, `bridge` (default), and user-created networks
- Simple network creation with custom CIDR
- Minimal state (just a map file)
- Focus on security and performance

## Network Types

### 1. `none` - No Network
```bash
# Most secure - no network access
rnx run bash "process_data.py"
```

### 2. `isolated` - External Access Only
```bash
# Can access external services only
rnx run --network=isolated wget "https://api.example.com/data"
```

### 3. `bridge` - Default Internal Network
```bash
# Default bridge network (172.20.0.0/16)
rnx run --network=bridge --name=api python "api.py"
rnx run --network=bridge curl "http://api:8080"
```

### 4. Custom Networks - User Defined
```bash
# Create custom network
rnx network create backend --cidr=10.1.0.0/24
rnx network create frontend --cidr=10.2.0.0/24

# Use custom network
rnx run --network=backend postgres
rnx run --network=backend python "app.py"
```

## Simple State Management

Network configurations only (persistent in `/opt/joblet/config/networks.json`):
```json
{
  "bridge": {
    "cidr": "172.20.0.0/16",

title: Build-packs Implementation
body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/ehsaniara/joblet/discussions/118
Originally posted by **ehsaniara** July 19, 2025 ## Basic Structure Every job now requires a buildpack, but all existing resource management and scheduling features remain: ```bash rnx run --buildpack= [resource-flags] [schedule-flags] [upload-flags] [args...] ``` ## Resource Management (Unchanged) ### CPU and Core Management ```bash # CPU percentage limiting with buildpack rnx run --buildpack=base-system --max-cpu=50 stress --cpu 4 # CPU core binding with buildpack rnx run --buildpack=java-17 --cpu-cores="0-3" java -jar app.jar # Single core allocation rnx run --buildpack=python-3.11 --cpu-cores="2" python compute.py # Complex core patterns rnx run --buildpack=base-system --cpu-cores="1,3,5,7" simulation_app rnx run --buildpack=node-18 --cpu-cores="0-1,4-5" node server.js # Combine CPU percentage + core binding rnx run --buildpack=java-17 --cpu-cores="2-3" --max-cpu=150 java -jar app.jar ``` ### Memory and I/O Limits ```bash # Memory limiting with buildpack rnx run --buildpack=python-3.11 --max-memory=1024 python data_processor.py # I/O bandwidth limiting rnx run --buildpack=base-system --max-iobps=10485760 dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/test bs=1M count=100 # All resource limits combined rnx run --buildpack=java-17 \ --max-cpu=75 \ --cpu-cores="0-1" \ --max-memory=2048 \ --max-iobps=5242880 \ java -Xmx1g -jar microservice.jar ``` ## Scheduling (Unchanged) ### Immediate vs Scheduled Execution ```bash # Immediate execution (default) rnx run --buildpack=base-system echo "Hello World" # Scheduled execution - relative time rnx run --buildpack=python-3.11 --schedule="1hour" python batch_job.py rnx run --buildpack=java-17 --schedule="30min" java -jar report_generator.jar rnx run --buildpack=node-18 --schedule="2h30m" node cron_task.js # Scheduled execution - absolute time rnx run --buildpack=python-3.11 --schedule="2025-07-18T20:02:48" python nightly_backup.py rnx run --buildpack=java-17 --schedule="2025-07-18T20:02:48Z" java -jar scheduled_task.jar ``` ### Scheduled Jobs with Resource Limits ```bash # Schedule a resource-intensive job for later rnx run --buildpack=python-3.11-data \ --schedule="tonight at 2am" \ --max-memory=8192 \ --cpu-cores="0-7" \ python ml_training.py # Schedule Java microservice with specific resources rnx run --buildpack=java-17-spring \ --schedule="1hour" \ --max-cpu=50 \ --cpu-cores="2-3" \ --max-memory=1024 \ java -jar microservice.jar ``` ## File Uploads (Unchanged) ### Single File Uploads ```bash # Upload single file with buildpack rnx run --buildpack=python-3.11 --upload=script.py python script.py rnx run --buildpack=java-17 --upload=app.jar java -jar app.jar # Multiple file uploads rnx run --buildpack=python-3.11 \ --upload=data.csv \ --upload=process.py \ python process.py ``` ### Directory Uploads ```bash # Upload entire directory rnx run --buildpack=node-18 --upload-dir=. npm start rnx run --buildpack=python-3.11 --upload-dir=ml-project python train.py # Upload with resource limits rnx run --buildpack=java-17 \ --upload-dir=./target \ --max-memory=2048 \ --cpu-cores="0-1" \ java -jar target/app.jar ``` ### Upload + Scheduling Combined ```bash # Schedule job with file uploads rnx run --buildpack=python-3.11-data \ --schedule="2hour" \ --upload-dir=dataset \ --max-memory=4096 \ --cpu-cores="2-5" \ python analyze_data.py # Schedule with single file upload and limits rnx run --buildpack=java-17 \ --schedule="30min" \ --upload=config.json \ --max-cpu=25 \ --cpu-cores="6" \ java -jar -Dconfig=config.json app.jar ``` ## Complete Real-World Examples ### Data Science Workload ```bash # Large dataset processing - scheduled for off-hours rnx run --buildpack=python-3.11-data \ --schedule="today at 11pm" \ --upload-dir=datasets \ --max-memory=16384 \ --cpu-cores="0-7" \ --max-iobps=104857600 \ python process_big_data.py ``` ### Java Microservice Deployment ```bash # Production microservice with precise resource allocation rnx run --buildpack=java-17-spring \ --upload=microservice.jar \ --upload=application.yml \ --max-cpu=100 \ --cpu-cores="2-3" \ --max-memory=1024 \ java -jar -Xmx512m microservice.jar ``` ### Machine Learning Training ```bash # GPU-accelerated training scheduled for later rnx run --buildpack=python-3.11-pytorch \ --schedule="2hour" \ --upload-dir=model \ --upload-dir=data \ --max-memory=8192 \ --cpu-cores="0-15" \ python train_model.py --epochs=100 ``` ### CI/CD Pipeline Job ```bash # Build and test job with time limits and resource constraints rnx run --buildpack=node-18 \ --upload-dir=. \ --max-cpu=200 \ --cpu-cores="4-7" \ --max-memory=2048 \ --max-iobps=52428800 \ bash -c "npm install && npm test && npm run build" ``` ### High-Performance Computing ```bash # Scientific simulation with dedicated cores rnx run --buildpack=base-system \ --upload=simulation.bin \ --upload-dir=input_data \ --cpu-cores="8-15" \ --max-memory=32768 \ ./simulation.bin --threads=8 --input=input_data/ ``` ## Buildpack Bundle Examples ### Bundle with All Features ```yaml # complex-workload-bundle.yml apiVersion: joblet.io/v1 kind: JobBundle metadata: name: "complex-ml-workload" spec: buildpack: name: "python-3.11-pytorch" version: "2.0.0" # Same resource management as CLI flags resources: memory: "8192Mi" # --max-memory=8192 cpu: "400m" # --max-cpu=400 cores: "0-7" # --cpu-cores="0-7" ioBPS: "104857600" # --max-iobps=104857600 # Scheduling support schedule: time: "2025-07-18T22:00:00" # --schedule="2025-07-18T22:00:00" # File upload equivalent files: - "./model/" # dest internally /work/model/ - "./data/" # dest internally /work/data/ - "./train.py" # dest internally /work/train.py application: entrypoint: ["python", "train.py"] args: ["--epochs=100", "--batch-size=32"] environment: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES: "0" PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF: "max_split_size_mb:512" ``` ### Using Bundle with Additional Overrides ```bash # Use bundle but override some settings rnx run --buildpack-bundle=complex-workload-bundle.yml \ --schedule="1hour" \ # Override bundle schedule --max-memory=16384 \ # Override bundle memory --upload=additional_data.csv # Add extra files # Immediate execution overriding scheduled bundle rnx run --buildpack-bundle=complex-workload-bundle.yml \ --schedule="" \ # Override to immediate execution --cpu-cores="0-3" # Override to fewer cores ``` ## Buildpack Management Commands ### Basic Buildpack Operations ```bash # List available buildpacks rnx buildpack list # Install new buildpack rnx buildpack install java-17:1.0.0 rnx buildpack install python-3.11-data:2.1.0 --from=registry.company.com # Show buildpack details rnx buildpack info java-17:1.0.0 # Remove unused buildpacks rnx buildpack prune ``` ### Status and Monitoring (Unchanged) ```bash # List all jobs (same as before) rnx list # Get job status with buildpack info rnx status # Stream logs (unchanged) rnx log # Stop running job (unchanged) rnx stop ``` ## Migration Examples ### Before (Old Joblet) ```bash # ❌ These won't work anymore rnx run echo "hello" rnx run --max-memory=1024 python script.py rnx run --schedule="1hour" --upload=data.csv python process.py ``` ### After (Buildpack-First) ```bash # ✅ Same functionality, explicit buildpack rnx run --buildpack=base-system echo "hello" rnx run --buildpack=python-3.11 --max-memory=1024 python script.py rnx run --buildpack=python-3.11 --schedule="1hour" --upload=data.csv python process.py # ✅ Or use convenience alias rnx run --base echo "hello" # --base is alias for --buildpack=base-system ``` ## Configuration Changes ### Auto-install Essential Buildpacks ```yaml # /opt/joblet/config/joblet-config.yml buildpacks: cacheDir: "/opt/joblet/buildpack-cache" autoInstall: - "base-system:1.0.0" # Essential for basic commands - "java-17:1.0.0" # Common runtime - "python-3.11:1.0.0" # Common runtime - "node-18:1.0.0" # Common runtime repositories: - name: "default" url: "https://buildpacks.company.com" ``` ## Summary **What Changes:** - All jobs must specify `--buildpack=` or use `--buildpack-bundle=` - Buildpacks replace the old host bind mount system **What Stays the Same:** - All resource flags: `--max-cpu`, `--max-memory`, `--max-iobps`, `--cpu-cores` - All scheduling: `--schedule` with relative/absolute time formats - All file uploads: `--upload` and `--upload-dir` - All monitoring: `rnx list`, `rnx status`, `rnx log`, `rnx stop` - All cgroup and namespace isolation - All security and process isolation features **Better Developer Experience:** - Predictable, versioned environments - Better reproducibility across different hosts - Clearer separation between environment (buildpack) and resources (flags) - Same powerful resource management with more reliable execution environments

title: fix(core): implement proper two-stage cgroup assignment
body:
Move cgroup assignment from host-side to init-stage to eliminate race condition where processes run without resource limits.

Changes:
- Add cgroup self-assignment in RunJobInit() before job execution
- Remove race-prone addProcessToCgroup() call from host side
- Add JOB_CGROUP_HOST_PATH environment variable for namespace/host path mapping
- Add cgroup assignment verification in init stage
- Fail job immediately if cgroup assignment fails

This fixes the critical security issue where jobs could run without requested resource limits due to timing gaps in process-to-cgroup assignment. The two-stage launch now works as originally designed: init process assigns itself to cgroup, then exec's the job command.

Before: Process starts → runs without limits → eventual assignment fails silently
After: Process assigns to cgroup → verifies assignment → exec's job with limits

Fixes resource limit bypass vulnerability where --max-cpu and other limits were silently ignored, allowing unlimited resource consumption.

Tested: CPU limits now work immediately upon job start
